newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may take flood credit from c.bank this week.
newsitem.headline: Poland may take flood credit from c.bank this week.

text.p: The Polish government may this week ask the National Bank of Poland for the first tranche of its 2.5 billion zloty ($719.4 million) flood relief credit, Andrzej Pilat, head of the government's flood relief office, told Reuters on Monday.
Pilat did not give any details on the terms of the loan but said that the central bank's role in financing the effort would be kept at a minimum.
"The first loan (from the central bank) may be made as early as the end of this week," Pilat said. "We want to take as little credit as possible from the NBP. We will borrow only when we need it."
Pilat said the government's credit needs will probably increase in the second half of August.
Last week the parliament passed a government proposal allowing the government to borrow an additional 2.5 billion zlotys from the central bank to finance flood relief.
Pilat said the government had already gathered about 3.5 billion zlotys ($1 billion) for flood relief outside of credit from the NBP.

He said about a third of this sum came from various budgetary reserves and the rest from credit given by international organisations, including $300 million from the World Bank and $70 million from the European Union's PHARE programme for Poland and Eastern Europe.
He said the government was still working on the exact framework of its flood aid expenditures as well as damage estimates from the two-weeks-old flood.
"We have already paid out 150 million zlotys in the first tranche...but the structure of further expenditures is still not decided at this moment," Pilat said.

He added however that the government already had enough funds to pay 3,000 zlotys to each of the estimated 60,000 households hit by the flooding, which had placed more than one percent of Poland underwater.
